notes: source.mutex.guard.v1 with card CT33-RANKS's opt-in lock-rank discipline. Two generations over disjoint resources are declared at ranks 1 and 2, and the case writes both nestings: `b` inside `a`, then `a` inside `b`. Only the descending acquisition is refused, at Q624 LockRankViolation naming both sides of the comparison that failed, and the exact ordered cascade [Q624, Q612] is pinned. The trailing Q612 DeadGuard is honest fallout rather than a second opinion: the refused Lock mints no guard, so the inner section's own unlock names a dead one, and pinning it is what shows the refusal neither released nor created a guard. The ascending_nesting.qcore control differs from the case by one statement — the second section nests `b` inside `a` again instead of the reverse — and is accepted through the checked mutex route, so the refusal is keyed to the acquisition order and not to nesting, to the two generations, or to the ranks being declared. The unranked.qcore control keeps the case's shape and replaces both `mutex rank N guards` declarations with `mutex guards`: it refuses with [Q622, Q622], one UnsupportedSynchronizationConstruct { NestedProtectingMutex } per nesting, which is the represented refusal that stood before this card and still stands — nesting is admitted only where a rank is declared, so an unranked module is unmoved. Only parse, elaborate, mutex_lowering and mutex_invariant_check execute; this route emits from a checked event list and has no CFG stage at all. NOT established: any native evidence. native_sanitized is unassessed, not executed — card CT33-RANKS does carry a sanitized native run of an equivalent ranked nested trace, but at the core level in crates/qcore-core/tests/unit/mutex_c_emit.rs rather than through this harness, and the schema-2 gate lists exactly which cases may read `executed`. evidence_target=linux records that an accepted control exists and is host-gated, NOT that any C was compiled or run. A passing rank check is not deadlock freedom: this model has no blocking at all, so no wait-for graph exists to argue over, and cross-task acquisition order is outside R2 entirely.
